subject: Netsuite renewal vs. vendor consolidation — recommendation needed
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T09:12:00Z
Subject: Netsuite renewal vs. vendor consolidation — ask + timeline

Team,

We need to decide whether to renew NetSuite for another 12 months or migrate invoicing to a dedicated billing provider (LedgerWorks or ChargeFlow) and consolidate expense tools. Procurement needs a recommendation by next week to start contracting.

Key constraints:
- NetSuite renewal quote arrives 2026-09-03; current contract ends 2026-09-30.
- Migration risk window: 6–8 weeks if we commit to a vendor now; that pushes cutover to late Oct.
- Finance prefers a single billing provider; Ops is wary of integrations.

Asks:
1) Marcus — can you confirm estimated engineering effort and whether we can run a parallel billing flow for 4 weeks?
2) Marissa — procurement: what procurement lead time / PO timelines look like for an add-on vs. new vendor (SOW + 3rd party vendor onboarding)?
3) Laura — legal: any hard blockers we should flag around data residency / SOC2 evidence for new vendor onboarding?

I've attached the initial vendor responses and the NetSuite renewal worksheet.

Thanks,

— Lauren
Head of Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: NetSuite_PRICING_Q3_2026.xlsx

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-31T11:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Netsuite renewal vs. vendor consolidation — ask + timeline

Lauren —

On Mon, Aug 30, 2026 at 09:12 Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team,
> 
> We need to decide whether to renew NetSuite for another 12 months or migrate invoicing to a dedicated billing provider (LedgerWorks or ChargeFlow) and consolidate expense tools. Procurement needs a recommendation by next week to start contracting.

Quick engineering readout: we can run a parallel billing flow for ~3–4 weeks but it requires:
- a) 2 senior backend engineers (approx 160h) for integrations (webhooks, idempotency, reconciliation)
- b) 1 SRE part-time for runbook and monitoring (40h)
- c) Feature toggles and reconciliation reports to be in place before cutover.

Estimated calendar impact: if we commit to a vendor by 9/7 and vendors deliver expected connectors, cutover earliest 10/18. If we renew NetSuite, minimal infra work but we should schedule a clean-up sprint for reconciliation issues (1 sprint).

Risk notes:
- LedgerWorks claims a native connector to our expense tool, but we need to validate edge-case refunds and tax-code mappings.
- ChargeFlow's connector is via ETL; expect additional delays for schema maturity.

I'll build a short engineering Impact doc and ping on Slack.

— Marcus
Director, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T15:23:00Z
Subject: Re: Netsuite renewal vs. vendor consolidation — ask + timeline

Lauren / Marcus,

Procurement perspective: short answers below.

Add-on (renew NetSuite + more seats / modules):
- Typical PO + contract amendment timeline: 7–12 business days after we approve pricing, assuming no legal redlines.
- No onboarding for vendor security; vendor already in our vendor registry.
- Cost: NetSuite renewal price (see attached sheet) is competitive if we only need billing and basic AR automation.

New vendor (LedgerWorks / ChargeFlow):
- SOW + onboarding + security review: 3–5 weeks minimum.
- Vendor onboarding checklist: SOC2 attestation, ISA/DPAs, vendor scanning (takes our security team ~5 business days after docs), procurement PO issuance: 10–15 business days after final SOW.
- If we need a reseller or marketplace contract (Azure/AWS), add 7–10 days for channel paperwork.

Recommendation for timeline: to meet the 9/30 contract lapse we need to either:
A) Approve NetSuite renewal by 9/07 to get PO out and invoice processed, or
B) Approve vendor selection + SOW by 9/01 and accelerate security reviews (marked as high priority) — this is tight and requires vendor cooperation and legal pre-clearance.

I'll coordinate with Finance Ops to queue the PO.

— Marissa
Procurement Manager
Redwood Inference

From: LedgerWorks Sales <sales@ledgerworks.com>

- Implementation: 6 weeks (project plan attached)
- Connector: Native integration with ExpensePlus (our tests show 98% match on refunds)
- Pricing: implementation fee $45k + $0.005 per invoice processed after first 500k/month included
- Security: SOC2 Type II report attached; we can sign Redwood's DPA with minimal edits.

Attachments: LedgerWorks_SOW_v3.pdf

Let us know if you'd like a revised SOW with milestone-based payments.

Regards,

Subject: Re: Netsuite renewal vs. vendor consolidation — recommendation + next steps

Team,

Thanks for the quick turn. Summary and recommendation:
- Engineering: feasible to run parallel for 3–4 weeks; estimated 200 engineering hours total (Marcus doc).
- Procurement: new vendor onboarding adds ~3–5 weeks; NetSuite renewal is fastest path to avoid gap (Marissa).
- Vendor capability: LedgerWorks appears to have stronger native connectors and a reasonable SOW; ChargeFlow is plausible but needs more ETL work.

Recommendation (pick one path):
1) Short-term (least risk): Approve NetSuite renewal through 9/30 to avoid operational risk. Simultaneously start a time-boxed migration evaluation with LedgerWorks as the preferred vendor and target an EOY pilot.
2) Aggressive (cost-first): Approve LedgerWorks now and accelerate onboarding — requires sign-off from Legal to fast-track SOC2/DPA review and a committed engineering sprint starting 9/13.

Please reply with your vote by EOD Friday 2026-09-10. If we go with #1 I will request the PO for NetSuite by 9/07. If we go with #2 I will inform LedgerWorks and push for milestone-based payments.

Next steps:
- Marcus: share engineering Impact doc in the BILL-342 ticket.
- Marissa: prepare PO timeline and draft SOW checklist.
- Laura: confirm if legal can expedite the DPA review (flagging data residency items if any).

— Lauren
Head of Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
